title: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war
summary:
Vice-President JD Vance sent shockwaves through Washington on Wednesday by blaming his party's midterm defeat squarely on the Iran war, in what was widely interpreted as an effort to distance himself from President Donald Trump ahead of a potential 2028 White House run.
In a carefully calibrated, 600-word statement on X, the vice-president acknowledged that Trump's 2024 voters had deserted Republicans in the midterm election.
In interviews late Tuesday night and Wednesday, Trump had defended the war but acknowledged that it played a factor in Democrats flipping control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate.
Vance's view on the war in Iran is an open secret in Washington.
But those disagreements had been kept out of the public eye - until now.

title: World leaders who sparred with Trump express relief mixed with caution at Republican election rout
summary:
LONDON (AP) — World leaders who have sparred with the "America first" President Donald Trump greeted the rout of his Republican Party in the U.S. midterm elections with a measure of relief Wednesday, allowing themselves to hope for a less combative U.S. foreign policy.
Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said the majority of Americans had sent a clear message that "they have had enough of MAGA and now want a different course.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Wednesday that Russia hoped Trump "will continue his peacemaking efforts" regardless of the election outcome.
A prominent German lawmaker urged Republicans to see the result in part as voters' verdict on Trump's "wrong foreign policy."

title: Melania Trump to host Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House
summary:
US First Lady Melania Trump is hosting Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House on Thursday, a day after being given Ukraine's highest award for women by President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The Order of Princess Olha, 1st Class, was awarded to Melania Trump for her "significant personal contribution to humanitarian support for Ukraine", according to the presidential decree.
The White House said that Melania Trump had "independently initiated engagement between the two warring nations and successfully secured a ceasefire".
Both the Russian and Ukrainian sides repeatedly thanked Melania Trump for brokering the ceasefire, though neither elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement.
On Thursday Melania Trump will also deliver remarks on the ceasefire in Oleshky at 11:00 (16:00 GMT), the White House website said.

title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
summary:
Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans voted "NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections.
Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices.
In an interview with Fox News, Trump said of the midterm results: "I think a part of it was Iran".
Speaking separately to the BBC's US news partner, CBS News, Trump said the conflict would end "when I say it ends".

title: Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock
summary:
In the election on 27 October, Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.
However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.
The role of Israel's president is largely ceremonial, but after an election they have the role of inviting a Knesset member to form a government.
The president also expressed confidence in the Shin Bet's ability to investigate the allegations of foreign interference in the election and appealed for patience.
